summary: Sessions 5 (fixtures) + 6 (openings) + 7 (trim) — backend persistence contract fully verified (5/5 pytest iter59, plus 4/4 iter58 regression still green). Frontend SHELL verified: enabling EDIT WALLS opens wall-editor-panel; the new wall-editor-add-door and wall-editor-add-window buttons exist and toggle their active style (bg-[#FFCC00] / bg-[#3a78d6]) on click, with the canvas cursor switching to 'crosshair' when active and reverting when toggled off. trim-takeoff-panel exists in the sidebar and renders a per-room table with trim-takeoff-row-{sheet.id}-{label_index} rows and a trim-takeoff-grand-total element. Trim tags PUT via the API persist across reload (17 LF door-casing baseline → 77 LF after tagging Baseboard+Crown on a 30 ft perimeter wall). Engine is exposed on window.__renderer_engine in non-prod with all required methods (setSelectedFixture, enableFixtureDrag, setFixtureRotation, setSelectedOpening, enableOpeningDrag, setAddOpeningMode). No React console errors, no TDZ / _createOpeningAt ReferenceError. Fixture-editor-card and opening-editor-card render paths could NOT be exercised end-to-end because engine.setSelectedFixture / setSelectedOpening only update the visual highlight — they do NOT invoke the useWallEditor pick callback that sets React state, so the cards never mount. This is a testability gap the review request implicitly assumed was covered; the product code path is correct on inspection.

integration_issues.issue: engine.setSelectedFixture(idx,sid), engine.setSelectedOpening(type,idx,sid), and engine.setAddOpeningMode(mode) are wired but only mutate scene highlight state. They do NOT invoke the enableWallEditor callback that sets useWallEditor's React state, so FixtureCard / OpeningCard never mount via the test hook. Real-user raycast picks still work in the browser. To make these Playwright-testable, expose a test-only pick-callback shim on window.__renderer_engine (e.g. engine.__test_firePick('fixture-pick', {fixture_index, sheet_id, kind, position_ft, size_ft, rotation_deg}) that calls the current wallEditorCallback), or expose the useWallEditor setters on window.__wall_editor. Similarly setAddOpeningMode('door') updates cursor+internal state but the click-to-place flow requires an actual canvas mousedown to hit the raycaster.

issues: Panel exits its empty-state hint as soon as ANY door/window sits on a wall that lies on a room-rect perimeter, even before the user tags any trim boolean. Example: fresh 30×20 room with a single 3 ft door already shows '17.0 LF total' and 1 row with only D.Cas populated. The review request said 'Before any trim is tagged, it shows the empty-state hint.' Consider gating the panel visibility on grandTotal-only-from-tagged-booleans > 0 (baseboard/crown/chair_rail sum > 0.5) instead of the current 'grandTotal including auto casings > 0.5'. Verify with product whether this is intended (auto door/window casings before user opts in).

action_items: Add a test-only pick hook on window.__renderer_engine so Playwright can drive FixtureCard/OpeningCard mounting deterministically (see integration_issues above).

Decide product behavior for TrimTakeoffPanel empty state: should auto door/window casings alone qualify a room as 'trimmed', or must at least one baseboard/crown/chair_rail boolean be set on that room's walls first?
sceneBuilder.js is now 2624 lines (was 2183 last iter). Split-file refactor is overdue; recommend factoring out per-layer builders and the wall-editor picking/callback logic.
critical_code_review_comments: sceneBuilder.js is 2624 lines — hard limit exceeded. Split into: sceneBuilder/index.js (orchestration), sceneBuilder/builders/*.js (per-layer), sceneBuilder/editor.js (picking, callbacks, drag handlers).

engine.setSelectedFixture / setSelectedOpening violate the principle of least surprise: they share names with useWallEditor.setSelectedFixture (which sets React state) but only do highlight. Either rename the engine variants (e.g. highlightFixture) or make them fire the pick callback so a single test-driven call path exists.

TrimTakeoffPanel._roomRectFt uses shadowing local `x0/x1/y0/y1` initialized from aabb but the reduction only ratchets values *toward* the label — for rooms that don't have both an X-crossing wall and a Y-crossing wall, this returns the full building AABB and every wall on the outer perimeter gets counted for the room. Works for a simple axis-aligned rectangular building; will over-count for L-shaped or multi-room layouts. Add unit tests for a 2-room house.

Door casing 17 LF / window casing 16 LF are hard-coded flat rates in TrimTakeoffPanel; the comment above admits per-unit rates should be derived from actual header height + width. Ship as v1 note in the sidebar footer already says as much.

useWallEditor._createOpeningAt is bound via a ref (createOpeningAtRef) to dodge TDZ. Works, but the pattern is fragile — adding a new mode later means remembering to also `useEffect(() => { createOpeningAtRef.current = _createOpeningAt })`. Consider inlining the add-opening handler inside the enableWallEditor useEffect instead of routing through an out-of-order forward ref.
